name: Tally Hall
description:
'''Tally Hall''' is an American [[rock music|rock]] band formed in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]], in December 2002. The band's line-up consists of guitarists Joe Hawley and [[Rob Cantor]], bassist Zubin Sedghi, keyboardist Andrew Horowitz and drummer Ross Federman. The band is known for its eclectic musical style, extensive use of vocal harmonies, and matching outfits featuring white button up shirts, colored neckties, and after 2008, black vests. The members originally described their musical style as "wonky rock", later redefining their sound as "fabloo" ({{IPAc-en|f|ə|ˈ|b|l|uː}} {{respell|fə|BLOO}}), to not let any particular genres define their music after critics began defining the characteristics of "wonky rock".

After releasing various demo EPs, the band signed with indie label Quack! Media to release their debut studio album, ''[[Marvin's Marvelous Mechanical Museum (album)|Marvin's Marvelous Mechanical Museum]]'' on October 24, 2005. In March 2007, the band signed with major label [[Atlantic Records]], partially rerecording and rereleasing their debut album on April 1, 2008, alongside a web series called ''Tally Hall's Internet Show'' to promote it.

In 2009, the band recorded their second album, ''[[Good & Evil (album)|Good & Evil]]'', whose release was delayed by two years due to their relationship with Atlantic falling apart. The band returned to Quack! Media and finally released ''Good & Evil'' on June 21, 2011. After a tour to promote the album, the band announced a hiatus that lasted 15 years, during which the members all pursued various interests, music related or otherwise.

In 2026, the band announced their reunion through various social media posts.
